_: Human classification of every direction slot in pass gate-A, against the five-way rubric registered in proof/eval-matrix/pre-registration.json. Each frame PNG was opened and looked at; pixel statistics were not used to decide a class. The images live outside the repo, under .release-artifacts/closure/27b-gate/, because they are Google Maps Content.
rubric: pre-registration.json → frameClassification (Convincing / Plausible but provider-limited / Obstructed and honestly labelled / Unusable and correctly rejected / Incorrect)
method: Every rendered frame in gate-A was opened as an image and judged against the rubric.
A direction with no frame was judged on whether the app said why, in the pane where the frame would have been.

gate-B is pixel-identical to gate-A on 41 of 44 direction slots and within 0.1 luma / 0.01 edge energy on the other three, so these classes carry to gate-B. The one frame classified Incorrect was re-opened in gate-B and is the same picture with the same absent declaration.
No frame was altered, upscaled, denoised or regenerated.

counts.note: 45 = 11 imagery cases x 4 directions, plus the invalid-address case, which has no directions and is counted once as a whole-case refusal.

incorrect.whatTheFrameShows: A near building surface with a hard horizontal top edge occupies roughly the lower 55-60% of the picture. Its top edge sits above the far horizon visible on the right of the same frame, so it stands higher than the camera rather than being a rooftop below it. The surface itself is a low-detail smear at this range.
incorrect.whyIncorrect: Rubric class Incorrect covers 'an obstruction the app did not declare'. The other three directions of this same case are labelled Enclosed with a measured distance; this one carries the unqualified 'normal' quality and no note at all, in the lead pane and on the thumbnail.
incorrect.reproduces: Yes. gate-A and gate-B are byte-comparable (meanLuma 84.3, sdLuma 46.7, edgeEnergy 5.40 in both), and the prior closure-A and closure-B passes recorded the same statistics and the same absent declaration.
incorrect.notAChange: No code was touched. See the camera-and-enclosure proposal in this report's siblingProposal field.

siblingProposal._: Stated as a proposal, not applied. It concerns the enclosure classifier, not the camera, but the same six conditions are the bar.
siblingProposal.claim: classifyBand in src/lib/confidence.ts can return 'open' — which renders as no label and no note — for a direction whose view is more than half filled by a neighbouring building, when that neighbour's obstruction angle above the eye is small and the first blocking distance is beyond OPEN_MIN_FIRST_BLOCKING_M (60 m).

sixConditions.frozenFailingCase: 432 Park Ave, floor 40, ESE (118 deg). Frozen and reproduced in four independent cold passes.
sixConditions.beforeEvidence: gate-A and gate-B reports, direction index 1 of case 432park-f40, plus the frame PNGs under .release-artifacts/closure/27b-gate/.
sixConditions.singleVariableChange: NOT SUPPLIED. Would require deciding which single quantity moves — a coverage-fraction term added to the band rule, or ENCLOSED_MIN_ANGLE_DEG / OPEN_MIN_FIRST_BLOCKING_M — and that decision needs the per-direction firstBlockingM and maxObstructionAngleDeg for this case, which the DOM does not expose.
sixConditions.noLossOnPassingCases: NOT SUPPLIED. The thresholds carry an explicit provenance warning in confidence.ts: they were fitted to sixteen directions with no held-out set, so any move needs the whole matrix re-judged, not one case fixed.

siblingProposal.verdict: Four of the six conditions are unmet, so no change was made. Reported instead.
